star. On two sides of the collar of the uniform the
following characters appear which are made of brass:-
Left side "Zao Ka Doo" (曹家渡)
Right side "Self Defence Corps" (自衛團)
Middle (about the position of the throat) "Number ".

Each person there has an armlet made of white cloth which
is carried on the left arm, and has the characters
imprinted "Zao Kao Doo Village Self Defence Corps: No....".
The three characters "Self Defence Corps" appear in a
round figure in the middle of the armlet while the remain-
ing characters "Zao Ka Doo Village" and "No...." above and
under them. The armlet also bears a chop which, however,
is illegible, having been treated with a black ink.

I discovered that one of the party, aged about 40,
height about 5'5", bore in the middle of the collar of his
uniform the characters "Pan Tsang" (班長) (section com-
mander) instead of a number carried by the other men.
He, nevertheless, has a number, "35", on the armlet.

In conversation with him it transpired that he is a
native of Anhwei and is the section commander of the
remaining 15 men. They were taken into custody by the
British Military several days ago while patrolling Brenan
Road.

11月15日下午1时许，我被英军士兵
拘禁在大西路（Great Western Road）英军营房的
讲堂内。

该房间内另有十六人
（中国人），均身着绿色制服并佩戴帽子。
帽子上饰有五角星形状的五色徽章。制服领口两侧
有下列黄铜制成的字符：-
左侧“曹家渡”
右侧“自衛團”
中间（约喉部位置）“编号”。

在场每人左臂均佩戴白布袖章，上面
印有字符“曹家渡村自卫团：第 ____ 号”。
袖章中央圆形图案内印有“自卫团”三字，其余
字符“曹家渡村”和“第 ____ 号”分别位于其上下方。
袖章上还盖有一枚印章，但因被黑墨涂抹，
无法辨认。

我发现其中一人，年龄约40岁，身高约5英尺5英寸，
其制服领口中间印有“班長”二字，而非其他人员
所佩戴的编号。尽管如此，他的袖章上仍有编号
“35”。

经与其交谈得知，他是安徽人，是其余
15人的班长。数日前，他们在布伦南路（Brenan Road）
巡逻时被英军拘捕。

- 2 -

While learning this, the sentry **〔此处转录不清〕** ordered me to stop talking with these men and instructed me to sit in the far corner, a distance of some 4 yards from them.

In compliance with the order, I remained silent but sat in the room listening to the conversation between the 16 men.

At about 2.00 p.m. one of the sixteen men, number 24, proceeded under escort of a British soldier to relieve nature and on his return I heard the British soldier accompanying him tell another British soldier in the room that the prisoner had had some conversation with a "boy" whom, I presumed, is employed in the Barracks and that he (the British soldier) was unable to understand the conversation. A little later I heard the person with the number, 24, inform his colleagues that the commander of the corps had sent a message to them (believed through the "boy" mentioned above) instructing them not to be too anxious because efforts were being made to secure their release within the next few days.

While I was sitting in the corner I made further endeavours to converse with the men whenever an opportunity offered and on one occasion when the section commander approached near me to obtain some tea, the tea-kettle being near me, I asked him as to the name of the commander and the object of their organization. He informed me that his commander's name is Wang and he is under the direct control of the "Shanghai City Government," the object of the organization being to keep an eye on the movements of the plain-clothes men of the Wang Ching Wei clique stationed in the Western District.

获悉此事时，哨兵 **〔此处转录不清〕** 命令我停止与这些人交谈，并指示我坐在远角，距离他们约4码处。

遵照命令，我保持沉默，但坐在房间里聆听这16人的谈话。

下午2时许，十六人中的第24号人员在一名英军士兵的押送下去解手，返回时，我听到陪同他的英军士兵告诉房间里的另一名英军士兵，该囚犯曾与一名“男孩”交谈，我推测该男孩受雇于营房，且他（该英军士兵）听不懂他们的谈话。稍后，我听到编号为24的人告知其同事，队长给他们传了话（据信是通过上述“男孩”），指示他们不必过于焦虑，因为正在努力争取在未来几天内释放他们。

当我坐在角落时，只要有机会，我便进一步尝试与这些人交谈。有一次，当班长走近我取茶时（茶壶在我附近），我询问他队长的姓名以及该组织的目的。他告诉我，他的队长姓王，直接受“上海市政府”管辖，该组织的目的是监视驻扎在西区的汪精卫派系便衣人员的动向。

From conversation amongst themselves, I also learned
that the majority of the members of the corps are Anhwei
natives all of whom have at least some direct or indirect
affiliation with the officers of the "Shanghai City Govern-
ment" Police Bureau.

I was called out from the room at about 4.30 p.m.
and released.

N.B.

The Zao Ka Doo Self Defence Corps also known as the
Zao Ka Doo Anti-Comintern Self Defence Corps, was formally
inaugurated on September 28, 1939 at No.93 Loo Sih Zah,
off Prenan Road, O.O.L., with one Woo Tuh San (胡德山)
as commander. It is under the direct control of the
Western Shanghai Administrative Office of the "Shanghai
City Government," 92 Jessfield Road, O.O.L.. The person
Wang, who is mentioned by the members of the corps now
detained in the British Military Barracks as "commander",
is possibly an officer directly in charge of the persons
being detained or may indicate Wang Tuh Ling (王德林),
Chief of the Western District Police Bureau, 11 & 13,
Jessfield Road, O.O.L..

Following the arrest of 13 members by the British Military on the morning of November 10, 1939, on Brenan Road, C.C.L., Woo Ah San (胡結山), Commander of the Shanghai Municipality Zoo Ke Doo Self Defence Corps (上海防共自衛隊), 33 Loo Sih Zah, Brenan Road, C.C.L., appealed to the Western Shanghai Administrative Office, "Shanghai City Government", which is the central organ of the Corps, for assistance.

Li Ta-tung (李達東), Chief of the Western Shanghai Administrative Office, requested the Japanese Gendarmerie of the Western District for assistance in securing the release of the 13 men but they have adopted an indifferent attitude for some reason unknown and up to the present have taken no steps to assist.

Fearing that the failure to obtain any assistance for the release of the arrested men may affect the morale of the corps, Woo Tuk San, Commander of the Corps, is now endeavouring to enlist the assistance of J. Akino (赤野), officer-in-charge of the Japanese Special Service Section at Lane 61/21 Kinnear Road, to intercede on his behalf with the Japanese Gendarmerie.

No reply has been received as yet as to whether his approach has been successful or not.

It is to be noted that members of this Corps were issued green coloured uniform and cape at the end of September, 1939.

继1939年11月10日上午，13名成员在中央捕房辖区（C.C.L.）极司菲尔路（Brenan Road）被英军逮捕后，上海特别市“捉狗”自卫队（Shanghai Municipality Zoo Ke Doo Self Defence Corps）指挥官胡结山（Woo Ah San），住址为中央捕房辖区极司菲尔路33号，向作为该队中枢机构的“上海市政府”沪西行政办事处求助。

沪西行政办事处主任李达东（Li Ta-tung）请求西区日本宪兵队协助释放这13人，但出于某种未知原因，日方态度冷淡，截至目前未采取任何协助行动。

由于担心无法获得协助以释放被捕人员可能会影响该队士气，该队指挥官胡德山（Woo Tuk San，音译，原文与上文 Woo Ah San 拼写不同）正努力争取金尼尔路（Kinnear Road）61/21弄日本特务机关负责人赤野（J. Akino）的协助，由其代表自己向日本宪兵队进行斡旋。

目前尚未收到关于其交涉是否成功的回复。

值得注意的是，该队成员于1939年9月底获发了绿色制服和斗篷。

Release Of
16 Chinese
By British

Band Freed On Proviso
That They Will Give
No Further Trouble

The British Military Authorities yesterday evening released the 16 armed Chinese who were arrested by patrols of the East Surrey Regiment on Brenan Road early in the morning of November 10, according to an official statement issued by the British Military Headquarters last night.

The men were released on the request of the Japanese adviser to the Shanghai City Government and Special Municipality Officials of the Western District, and on the receipt of a written undertaking by the British Military Authorities that the Defence Corps to which these Chinese belonged had been disbanded and would cause no further trouble in the future.

The 16 armed Chinese were arrested and then detained last Friday by a patrol party of the East Surreys who encountered the men proceeding along Brenan Road in a rambling, aimless manner. On being told that they could not proceed into the Settlement bearing arms and dressed in uniforms, the 16 men surrendered themselves and their weapons without resistance and were taken to the British military camp on Great Western Road. They were kept there till yesterday evening when negotiations for their release were finally completed.

Official Statement

The official statement issued by the British Military Authorities last night follows:—

“The 16 armed Chinese arrested by the British Military Authorities on November 10 were released to-night after a request had been made by the Japanese advisor to the Shanghai City Government and Special Municipality Officials of the Western District.

“The Special Municipality Officials and the Japanese adviser have given a written undertaking that the Za Ka Doo Defence Corps, to which these men belonged, has now been disbanded, and they will therefore cause no further trouble in the future.

“The rifles, pistols and hand-grenades carried by these men have been confiscated by the British Military Authorities.”

据英国军事总部昨晚发布的官方声明，萨里郡东团（East Surrey Regiment）巡逻队于11月10日凌晨在极司菲尔路（Brenan Road）逮捕的16名武装中国人，已于昨晚被英军当局释放。

这些人是在上海市政府顾问及西区特别市官员的请求下获释的，且英军当局收到了一份书面保证，称这些中国人所属的自卫队已经解散，将来不会再制造麻烦。

这16名武装中国人是上周五被萨里郡东团的一支巡逻队逮捕并拘留的，当时巡逻队遇到这些人漫无目的地沿着极司菲尔路行进。当被告知他们不能携带武器并穿着制服进入租界时，这16人未作抵抗，交出了自己和武器，随后被带往大西路（Great Western Road）的英军营房。他们一直被关押在那里，直到昨晚释放谈判最终完成。

官方声明

以下是英军当局昨晚发布的官方声明：—

“11月10日被英军当局逮捕的16名武装中国人，在上海市政府顾问及西区特别市官员提出请求后，于今晚获释。

“这些人携带的步枪、手枪和手榴弹已被英军当局没收。”

CHINA PRESS.

NOV 15 1939

16 Men Held By East Surreys
Stage 24-Hour Hunger Strike

Resistance Breaks Down After First Day Of
Going Without Food And Men Return
To Normal Eating Routine

The 16 mysterious and unwant-
ed "walking arsenals" arrested last
Friday on Brenan Road by the East
Surreys dislike detention so much
that gave evidence of their dis-
pleasure by going on a hunger
strike over the weekend.

The hunger strike started Sunday
morning when the "War babies" in-
formed their jailors that they
would forego eating until such time
as they might be released. The
East Surreys offered no objections
whereupon the men proceeded to
carry out their resolution.

This firm resolve to starve them-
selves until release was forthcom-
ing carried through the noon hour.
When dinner time arrived, the 16
prisoners still refused to eat but
some of them were looking rather
peaked. By breakfast time on
Monday, their resistance to offers
of food had broken down and so
had their determination to stay on

a starvation diet. A hunger strike
of 24 hours had come to a sudden
end.

Both Sides Growing Tired

Still unclaimed, the 16 "orphans
of the storm" were being held in
detention by the East Surreys last
night. Both the Surreys and the
detained men were reported to be
growing tired of the game but there
seems to be nothing that either
side could do about effecting a re-
lease. The British military auth-
orities have decided to wait a few
more days for the owners of the
green-uniformed "gunmen" to show
up before making arrangements to
dispose of the case.

When arrested, the 16 were
literally walking arsenals. They
were equipped with rifles, pistols,
hand-grenades and ammunition.
They were disarmed and lock up.

The British military authorities
subsequently let it be known that
they had possession of the men with
the hope that some organization
would come forward and claim
them. But up to the present time,
no claim has been put forward and
some doubt was expressed by the
East Surreys last night that such a
claim will be forthcoming.

From Anhwei

According to the story told by
the men, they arrived in the Shang-
hai area about 10 days ago from
Anhwei. But apparently, even
they do not know just who they
are working for. Some one gave
them uniforms, guns and grenades
of the potato-masher type and told
them to go and find a street to
patrol. They selected Brenan Road
and were consequently picked up
by the East Surreys.

The uniforms they wear are not
of the type worn by the "Ta Tao"
policeman, nor of the same style
and color worn by Wang Ching-
wei's so-called "Self Protection
Corps," or any other organization
sponsored by Wang or the "Special
Shanghai Municipality" authorities.

（批：Liu C%）

1939年11月15日

萨里郡东团扣押16人
上演24小时绝食抗议

断食首日过后抵抗瓦解
众人恢复常规饮食

上周五在极司菲尔路（Brenan Road）被萨里郡东团逮捕的16名神秘且不受欢迎的“行走军火库”，因极度厌恶拘留，在周末通过绝食来表达他们的不满。

绝食始于周日早晨，当时这些“战争婴儿”告知狱卒，他们将停止进食，直到获释为止。萨里郡东团未加反对，于是这些人便开始执行他们的决定。

这种坚决绝食直至获释的决心一直持续到中午。到了晚餐时间，16名囚犯仍拒绝进食，但其中一些人看起来面色相当憔悴。到了周一早餐时间，他们对食物提供的抵抗已经瓦解，坚持饥饿饮食的决心也随之崩溃。一场持续24小时的绝食突然结束。

双方均感疲惫

昨晚，这16名“风暴孤儿”仍无人认领，被萨里郡东团拘留。据报道，萨里郡团和被拘留者都对这场博弈感到厌倦，但似乎双方都无法采取有效措施促成释放。英军当局决定再等几天，看这些身穿绿色制服的“枪手”的主人是否会现身，然后再安排处理此案。

被捕时，这16人简直是“行走的军火库”。他们装备有步枪、手枪、手榴弹和弹药。他们被解除武装并关押起来。

随后，英军当局透露，他们扣留这些人，是希望有某个组织能出面认领。但截至目前，尚无人提出认领，萨里郡东团昨晚表示怀疑是否会有人来认领。

来自安徽

据这些人讲述的故事，他们大约10天前从安徽抵达上海地区。但显然，连他们自己也不知道究竟在为谁工作。有人给了他们制服、枪支和土豆捣碎器式（potato-masher type，指木柄手榴弹）的手榴弹，并让他们去找一条街道巡逻。他们选择了极司菲尔路，结果被萨里郡东团抓获。

他们穿着的制服既不是“大道”（Ta Tao，音译，可能指伪警或特定派系）警察所穿的那种，也不是汪精卫所谓“自卫队”或其他由汪精卫或“上海特别市”当局赞助的组织所穿的相同款式和颜色的制服。

（批注：刘 C%）

NOV 1 1 1939

East Surreys Detain
Armed Chinese

Band Walking in British
Defence Sector Held Up

Sixteen armed and uniformed Chi-
nese who were seen walking inside
the British defence area in the
western district yesterday at about
7 a.m. were stopped near Brenan
Road by a patrolling party of the
East Surrey Regiment. They carried
rifles and hand grenades. They were
disarmed and still detained late last
night pending their identification.
It was ascertained last night that
the detained persons have nothing
to do whatsoever with Mr. Wang
Ching-wei's corps with headquarters
in Jessfield Road. It was learned that
members of the corps would never
be allowed to walk freely in the
street while carrying firearms.
It was reported that the detained
men were alleged to have extorted
some money from a Chinese shop
near Brenan Road and that when
they were leaving after obtaining
some $6 they were met by the British
soldiers. The report could not be
confirmed, however.

萨里郡东团拘留
武装中国人

在英军防区行走的
一伙人被拦下

昨天早上7点左右，在西区英军防区内被发现行走的16名身穿制服且携带武器的中国人，在极司菲尔路附近被萨里郡东团的一支巡逻队拦下。他们携带步枪和手榴弹。他们被解除武装，截至昨晚深夜仍被拘留，以待确认身份。
昨晚查明，被拘留者与总部设在杰斯菲尔德路（Jessfield Road，即兆丰公园路/中山公园路）的汪精卫先生的部队毫无关系。据悉，该部队成员绝不会被允许携带枪支在街上自由行走。
有报道称，被拘留者涉嫌在极司菲尔路附近的一家中国商店勒索了一些钱财，他们在拿到约6元钱离开时遇到了英国士兵。然而，该报道未能得到证实。

SHANGHAI TIMES.

NOV 1 1 1939

East Surreys
Disarm Band
Of Sixteen

Marching On Brenan Rd.
In British Defence
Area Yesterday

BEING HELD BY BRITISH
UNTIL IDENTIFIED

Dressed in green but some-
what irregular uniforms, a
band of 16 armed Chinese were
arrested and detained by patrols
of the East Surrey Regiment in
Brenan Road at 7 o'clock yes-
terday morning, an official of
the British Military Headquar-
ters informed "The Shanghai
Times" yesterday.
The men were seen, marching
along Brenan Road in a rambling
manner and were approached by
men from Posts in this sector. They
were ordered to halt and informed
that they could not proceed into
the Settlement bearing arms and
dressed in uniforms. When order-
ed to do so, the group of men
peacefully surrendered their arms
to the military without creating any
incident or offering resistance. An
officer was called to the scene and
the band of men were taken into
custody to the British military
camp on Great Western Road.
Up until late last night, no auth-
ority appeared to identify the de-
tained men, and they were still be-
ing held in custody. It is not
known to what organization the
men belong or exactly what there
intentions were in marching into
the International Settlement bear-
ing arms. The men were carrying
rifles, pistols and hand grenades.
Orderly Conduct
Meanwhile the group of men are
being fed and quartered at the
camp. It is stated that the men
ate heartily yesterday and were
conducting themselves in an order-
ly manner under the military con-
trol. When an official appears to
answer for the men they will be
turned over to him, it was stated.
There are no facilities for keeping
men at this camp for any duration
of time.
No one has appeared as yet to
claim the men or make any ex-
planations. It is expected, how-
ever, that the matter will be settled
to-day and the men released from
the military camp.

1939年11月11日

萨里郡东团
解除16人
武装团伙

昨日在英军防区
极司菲尔路行进

由英方扣留
直至身份确认

英国军事总部的一位官员昨天告诉《上海泰晤士报》，昨天早上7点，一伙16名身穿绿色但略显不规范制服的武装中国人在极司菲尔路被萨里郡东团的巡逻队逮捕并拘留。
这些人被看到沿极司菲尔路漫无目的地行进，该防区哨所的士兵上前接近。他们被命令停下，并被告知他们不能携带武器并穿着制服进入租界。当接到命令时，这群人和平地向军方缴械，没有引发任何事件或进行抵抗。一名军官被召至现场，这伙人被带往大西路（Great Western Road）的英军营房拘押。
直到昨晚深夜，尚无当局出面确认被拘留者的身份，他们仍被羁押。目前尚不清楚这些人属于什么组织，也不清楚他们携带武器进入国际租界的确切意图。这些人携带步枪、手枪和手榴弹。
行为有序
与此同时，这群人在营房内得到食宿供应。据说这些人昨天吃得很饱，在军方控制下表现有序。据悉，一旦有官员出面为这些人负责，他们将被移交给该官员。该营房没有长期关押人员的设施。
截至目前，尚无人出面认领这些人或作出任何解释。不过，预计此事将于今天解决，这些人将从军营获释。

ATTEMPT BY JAPANESE AND S.C.G.P.B. TO ENTER
BRITISH HOUSE O.O.L.

At 11.15 a.m. 20/10/39 a telephone message was
received from Mr. F.C. Roberts, 68 Tifeng Road, report-
ing that members of the S.C.G.P. Bureau accompanied by
Japanese had attempted to enter the house of his mother-
in-law, Mrs. S. Talbot, at No.9 Great Western Road.

No.9 Great Western Road is a large house situated
at the south-west corner at the intersection of Great
Western and Tifeng Roads, and is O.O.L. It is occupied
by Mrs. S. Talbot and her son Mr. G. Talbot. In an
erection on the north side of the house is a factory
making the well known Talbot cholera medicine "S Tah Ts
(施德之)". All members of the Talbot family are
British Subjects and Eurasians. The house is registered
at H.B.M. Consulate as British property under Notifica-
tion No.336 dated 13/12/37, and a copy of it in English,
Chinese and Japanese is displayed in the hall of the
house.

At about 10.30 a.m. 20/10/39, during the absence
of Mrs. S. Talbot and her son, a party of men comprising
two Japanese in plain-clothes, a Chinese in civilian
clothes and a uniformed member of the S.C.G.P. Bureau,
entered the drive of No.9 Great Western Road by one of
them inserting his hand and opening the bolt of the gate.

Zao Ka Doo Anti-Comintern Self Defence Corps - demand
financial aid from factories in Western District
------------------------------------------------------------------

The Zao Ka Doo Anti-Comintern Self Defence
Corps, 93 Loo Sih Zah, off Brenan Road, O.O.L.,
recently assigned a representative named Wong Dien Siang
(王殿湘), to call on factories situated in Loo Sih
Zah, off Brenan Road, and South Zao Ka Zah, off
Edinburgh Road, O.O.L., to demand financial aid.
Large factories will be required to contribute $200.00
each while small factories $100.00 each. The money
thus raised, the representative claimed, will be used
to purchase firearms for the corps in order that the
latter can better protect the people in the area.

Numerous factories in the district are
negotiating with the corps either directly or
indirectly for a reduction in the contribution.

Certified true copy
J. F. Lovell

WPY/.

Sir;

On the 20-10-39 Mr. C.J. Doughty came to the Station and reported that two members of the Self Defence Corps had again visited his factory No.30 Brenan Road, with view to soliciting a subscription.

They were offered $20.00 however this they refused, stating that a large firm like C.J. Doughty's should be able to subscribe anything from $100.00 to $200.00 adding that they had 4 rates, i.e. $300.00, $200.00, $100.00 & $50.00 which depended on the size of the business. Mr. Doughty then told these men that his firm would donate $50.00 but that since his accountant had been robbed no cash was kept at the factory, but if they would send some one on the 21-10-39 would give them a cheque, they agreed to accept this amount and said they would send someone on the 21-10-39 to collect the cheque, whereupon Mr. Doughty asked to whom should the cheque be made payable and was given a visiting card bearing the name Ma Hoong Sung (馬轟申) "Captain of the 3rd Branch, 1st Squad, Anti Communistic Self Defence Corps, Zau Ka Doo Village, Shanghai West (滬西曹家渡鎮防共自衛團第一中隊第三分隊長), Yangchow, Kiangsu.

These two persons then said they understood Mr. Doughty kept 2 pistols at the factory, to which he replied in the affirmative, they then said that a pistol would be more acceptable than the money and would take one in lieu, however Mr. Doughty refused to consider the suggestion.

D. S. I.

Made by D.S.I. Burton Forwarded by J. McFarlane

Sir;
On the 17-10-39 Mr. C.J. Doughty of No.30 Brenan Rd
O.J.L. came to the Station and stated that at about
10.30 a.m. 17-10-39 3 male Chinese two in civilian
clothes and one in a green coloured uniform, called at
the above address which is the firm of C.J. Doughty & Co.
Engineers and through the medium of an interpreter which
they borrowed from the S.M.P. Bureau Sub Station on
Brenan Road adjacent to Mr. Doughty's factory, stated
that they were members of the newly formed Western
District Volunteers and that they were soliciting for
donations from all factories east of the railway line
with view to raising a sum of $10,000.00 which sum will
be utilized to supply uniforms and arms for the
volunteer members, the idea being to commence with 100
men and gradually increase the strength.
The two men in civilian clothes styled themselves
as Captains whilst the man in uniform was taken to show
the type of uniform that will be worn by this group.
They further went on to say that their object was
to protect all factories, etc., east of the railway line
to the Settlement Boundary and north from the French
Boundary to the Soochow Creek.
They intimated that donations of any denomination
would be gratefully accepted, but suggested that Mr.
Doughty's firm should donate at least $100.00. It is
understood that these volunteers being sponsored by Lee
Shih Chuen (李自群) who has appointed one Woo Tuh San
(胡德山) as their leader.

D.S.I. Kuh

〔正文内容〕
A "Shanghai Municipality Zao Ka Doo Self Defense Corps" (上海特別市沪西曹家渡自衛團) was formally inaugurated on the morning of September 28, 1939 in the Zao Nan Primary School, No. 93 Loo Sih Zah, off Brenan Road, O.O.L..

This corps has a total of 85 members who are armed with some 20 rifles and 15 Mauser pistols. They wear a sort of greenish uniform and hats each bearing a five-coloured emblem in the form of a star. It is said that they are issued a monthly pay of $30.00 each. The commander is one Woo Tuh San (胡德山), who is a native of Anhwei and an ex-soldier.

This corps, being a local militia corps, is formed under the auspices of the Zao Ka Doo Guild which is situated in the Zao Nan Primary School, 93 Loo Sih Zah, off Brenan Road, O.O.L., but is subject to the supervision of the Western District Section of the Japanese Military Police, 94 Jessfield Road, O.O.L.. A representative of the latter attends the office of the corps daily and assists Woo Tuh San, the commander, in controlling and training the members.

It will be noted that members of this corps were responsible for the robbery of 3 service pistols from 3 C.P.C.s on duty at the corner of Connaught and Jessfields, in the evening of September 15, 1939.

C. 30/9.

Liao Chung Chien
D. S. I.

D. C.(Special Branch).

该团共有成员85名，配备约20支步枪和15支毛瑟手枪。他们身着一种绿灰色制服，帽子上饰有五角星形状的五色徽章。据悉，每人月薪为30.00元。团长为胡德山 (Woo Tuh San)，安徽人，前军人。

该团作为地方民团，是在位于越界筑路区白利南路旁罗师庄93号曹南小学的曹家渡公会主持下成立的，但受位于越界筑路区极司菲尔路94号的日本宪兵队西区分部监管。后者的一名代表每日前往该团办公处，协助团长胡德山管理和训练成员。
